claim: Best window to visit is the dry-ish season March–September; firefly cruises run year-round.
The NE monsoon (Nov–Feb) makes Sabah's north coast and the Tip of Borneo wet and choppy; best March–September.
June 2026 exchange rate RM1 ≈ €0.21 / €1 ≈ RM4.7.
Sabah Parks banned single-use plastic bags across all parks from 1 Jan 2026; Poring has a canopy walk and hot springs.
Grab from KK airport to the centre is RM15–35 (~€3–7); the centre is walkable.
KL (KUL) to KK (BKI) is a ~2h40m direct flight from around €50 one-way.
The City 'Floating' Mosque is KK's signature postcard, best at golden hour.
Tanjung Aru's sunset is rated among Southeast Asia's best.
Gaya Street hosts a Sunday market that is the heart of central KK.
Sabah's noodle canon — ngiu chap (beef noodle), sang nyuk mee (pork noodle) and Tuaran mee — are the local must-eats.
The Filipino Market waterfront stalls let you grill your own seafood at dusk.
Tunku Abdul Rahman Park is five islands ~15–20 min by boat from town — Malaysia's first marine park and the best easy day out of KK.
Boats to the marine park leave from Jesselton Point jetty, nearest island ~15 min out.
Kinabalu Park is Malaysia's only natural UNESCO World Heritage Site; Mount Kinabalu rises to 4,095 m.
Kinabalu Park offers botanical and nature trails enjoyable without the permit-and-overnight summit climb.
The Klias river cruise reliably delivers proboscis monkeys and fireflies.
Kiulu offers gentle Grade I–II white-water rafting suitable for beginners.
Mari Mari Cultural Village is the polished introduction to Sabah's indigenous peoples.
Monsopiad Cultural Village houses 42 real headhunter skulls.
Gaya Island Resort is a character splurge stay 15 min by boat off the marine park.
The Jesselton Hotel (1954) is the city's one genuine heritage room.
The Sabah State Museum complex (entry RM15) is a primer on the state's cultures.
Kaamatan, the Kadazan-Dusun harvest festival, has its state finale 30–31 May 2026 at KDCA Penampang.
KK to Sandakan is a 45-minute flight, far better than the ~6-hour mountain bus.
